framework: AWS Well-Architected Framework Security Pillar + CIS AWS Benchmark
description: Internet Exposure Assessment - Identifies all resources exposed to the internet, maps complete architecture chains, and evaluates misconfiguration and attack surface risks

items.title: S3 buckets with sensitive data must not be publicly accessible
items.description: S3 buckets containing backups, logs, PII, or customer data exposed publicly. AllUsers ACL or IsPublic policy allows unrestricted read/list access from internet.
items.remediation: Enable Block Public Access at bucket level: aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket BUCKET --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true

pci_dss.reason: This control requires restricting access to cardholder data (storage, transmission, deletion). Public S3 buckets with customer/payment data directly violate this requirement.
This control addresses broken access control. Public S3 buckets are a classic example of broken access control allowing unauthorized access to sensitive data.
This control requires retention of audit trail records. Public S3 buckets expose historical data without audit controls, violating retention policies.

items.title: Security Groups must not allow SSH (22) access from 0.0.0.0/0
items.description: EC2 instances with SSH access open to entire internet. Exposed to brute-force attacks, vulnerability exploitation, and unauthorized access.
items.remediation: Restrict SSH to specific IPs or use Systems Manager Session Manager: aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id SG_ID --protocol tcp --port 22 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0 && aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id SG_ID --protocol tcp --port 22 --cidr <OFFICE_IP>/32

pci_dss.reason: This control requires restricting inbound traffic to only necessary, approved traffic and denying all other traffic. SSH open to internet violates the deny-by-default principle.
This control mandates limiting access to system components to only those individuals requiring access. SSH open to 0.0.0.0/0 allows unrestricted access.

items.title: Security Groups must not allow RDP (3389) access from 0.0.0.0/0
items.description: Windows instances with RDP exposed to internet. Critical risk for brute-force and credential-based attacks.
items.remediation: Restrict RDP to specific office IPs: aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id SG_ID --protocol tcp --port 3389 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0

pci_dss.reason: This control requires restricting inbound traffic to only necessary traffic and denying all other. RDP exposed to internet violates this principle.

items.title: Security Groups must not expose database ports (3306, 5432, 1433, 27017) to 0.0.0.0/0
items.description: Database ports directly accessible from internet. Allows unauthorized database access, SQL injection attacks, and data exfiltration.
items.remediation: Remove database port rules from 0.0.0.0/0. Database ports should only be accessible from application servers: aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id SG_ID --protocol tcp --port 3306 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0

pci_dss.reason: Exposing database ports to internet violates the deny-by-default inbound traffic principle.
Direct database exposure violates access restriction requirements for cardholder data.

items.title: RDS instances must not have PubliclyAccessible enabled
items.description: RDS database instances with PubliclyAccessible=true allow connections from internet. Should only be accessible from application servers in private subnet.
items.remediation: Disable public accessibility and ensure database is in private subnet: aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier DB_ID --no-publicly-accessible --apply-immediately

pci_dss.reason: Public RDS directly violates the principle of restricting inbound traffic to only necessary sources.
Publicly accessible databases expose cardholder data to internet access.

items.title: Lambda functions with public URLs must have authentication enabled
items.description: Lambda functions with Function URLs accessible without authentication. AuthType=NONE allows anyone to invoke the function, potentially accessing sensitive data or performing unauthorized actions.
items.remediation: Enable authentication for Lambda URLs: aws lambda update-function-url-config --function-name FUNCTION_NAME --auth-type AWS_IAM or use AWS_IAM with resource-based policy

pci_dss.reason: Public Lambda URLs without authentication allow unrestricted access to functions, violating access control requirements.

items.title: API Gateway endpoints must have authentication configured
items.description: API Gateway REST/HTTP APIs accessible without authentication (no API key, IAM, Cognito, or custom authorizer). Allows unauthorized API consumption, data access, and abuse.
items.remediation: Implement authentication. Option 1 (API Key): aws apigateway create-api-key --name prod-key --enabled. Option 2 (IAM): Update resource policy. Option 3 (Cognito): Attach user pool to API.

pci_dss.reason: APIs without authentication allow unrestricted access, violating least privilege principles.
Authentication is required for user identification and is a fundamental security control.

items.title: Lambda environment variables must not contain hardcoded credentials
items.description: Secrets, passwords, API keys, database credentials stored in Lambda environment variables. Anyone with Lambda:GetFunction permission can read plaintext credentials.
items.remediation: Migrate credentials to AWS Secrets Manager: aws secretsmanager create-secret --name prod/lambda/db-password --secret-string '{"password":"xxx"}' --kms-key-id KMS_KEY_ID. Update Lambda to retrieve secret at runtime.

pci_dss.reason: Hardcoded credentials in source/environment violate secure credential management requirements.
This control requires strong authentication mechanisms. Hardcoded credentials weaken authentication.

items.title: Application Load Balancers must have WAF attached for production applications
items.description: Internet-facing ALBs without AWS WAF protection. Applications vulnerable to OWASP Top 10 attacks (SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, etc.), bots, and credential stuffing.
items.remediation: Create WAF Web ACL and associate with ALB: aws wafv2 create-web-acl --name prod-waf --scope REGIONAL --default-action Allow={} --rules file://waf-rules.json --visibility-config SampledRequestsEnabled=true,CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true,MetricName=prod-waf. Then: aws wafv2 associate-web-acl --web-acl-arn ARN --resource-arn ALB_ARN

pci_dss.reason: This control requires protecting web applications from known attacks. WAF is essential for detecting and blocking OWASP Top 10 attacks.

items.title: API Gateway must have throttling/rate limiting configured
items.description: API Gateway without throttling allows unlimited requests. Vulnerable to DoS attacks, abuse, and cost overruns from malicious API consumption.
items.remediation: Configure usage plan with throttling: aws apigateway create-usage-plan --name prod-plan --throttle burstLimit=1000,rateLimit=500. Update stage: aws apigateway update-stage --rest-api-id API_ID --stage-name prod --patch-operations op=replace,path=/throttle/rateLimit,value=1000

pci_dss.reason: This control requires protecting applications from broken access control. Rate limiting helps prevent abuse and ensures fair resource usage.

items.title: CloudFront distributions must have AWS Shield Standard enabled (default) and Shield Advanced evaluated
items.description: CloudFront distributions without DDoS protection. Applications vulnerable to volumetric and application-layer DDoS attacks.
items.remediation: Shield Standard is enabled by default. For critical applications, subscribe to Shield Advanced: aws shield subscribe --subscription. Alternative: Use AWS WAF on CloudFront distribution.

pci_dss.reason: This control requires protection of internet-facing resources. DDoS protection (Shield) is essential for maintaining availability.

items.title: ALB/NLB listeners must use TLS 1.2+ (not TLS 1.0/1.1)
items.description: Load balancer listeners using obsolete TLS versions (1.0, 1.1) with weak ciphers. Vulnerable to known cryptographic attacks (POODLE, BEAST, etc.).
items.remediation: Update SSL policy to TLS 1.2+. Recommended policy: ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06 or ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017-01: aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn LISTENER_ARN --ssl-policy ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06

pci_dss.reason: This control requires strong cryptography. TLS 1.2+ is mandatory for secure data transmission. TLS 1.0/1.1 are considered weak.

items.title: Security Groups should minimize overly broad port ranges
items.description: Security groups with ranges like 0-65535 or excessive port ranges allow unintended access. Violates least privilege principle.
items.remediation: Replace broad rules with specific ports. Review each rule and restrict to minimum necessary: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id SG_ID --protocol tcp --port SPECIFIC_PORT --source-security-group-id SG_SOURCE

pci_dss.reason: This control requires denying all inbound traffic by default and allowing only necessary services. Broad port ranges violate this.

items.title: S3 bucket object listing must not be publicly accessible
items.description: S3 buckets where ListBucket permission is granted to AllUsers/Principal: '*'. Attackers can enumerate all objects in bucket, finding sensitive data.
items.remediation: Remove ListBucket permission from bucket policy or restrict to authenticated users: Remove statement with Principal: '*' and s3:ListBucket action

pci_dss.reason: Allowing public bucket listing violates access restriction to cardholder data.

items.title: Lambda functions must have least privilege IAM role attached
items.description: Lambda functions with overly permissive IAM roles (e.g., AdministratorAccess, full service permissions). If compromised, attacker gains excessive permissions.
items.remediation: Review Lambda IAM role and restrict to minimum necessary permissions. Remove wildcard permissions: aws iam delete-role-policy --role-name ROLE_NAME --policy-name POLICY_NAME. Attach specific managed policies or create custom policy.

pci_dss.reason: This control requires access based on least privilege. Lambda roles should only have permissions for specific actions.

items.title: EC2 instances in public subnet should be behind load balancer (not directly internet-facing)
items.description: EC2 instances in public subnet with public IPs directly exposed. Better practice is to have instances in private subnet behind ALB/NLB.
items.remediation: Create ALB and move EC2 instances to private subnet targets. This requires migration planning: 1) Create ALB in public subnets 2) Create target group pointing to instances 3) Gradually migrate to private subnet instances

pci_dss.reason: Direct instance exposure violates network segregation best practices. Load balancers provide additional security layer.

items.title: Network ACLs should not have overly permissive inbound rules (0.0.0.0/0)
items.description: NACLs with broad Allow rules on inbound traffic. While Security Groups are primary defense, permissive NACLs reduce defense-in-depth.
items.remediation: Review NACL rules and restrict to necessary CIDR blocks. Remove overly broad rules and add specific rules for required traffic.

pci_dss.reason: NACLs should follow deny-by-default principle, allowing only necessary inbound traffic.

items.title: CloudFront distributions must use Origin Access Identity (OAI) for S3 origins
items.description: CloudFront serving S3 content without OAI. Users can bypass CloudFront and access S3 directly using bucket URL, bypassing caching and security controls.
items.remediation: Configure Origin Access Identity for S3 origins: 1) Create OAI 2) Update bucket policy to allow only OAI 3) Update CloudFront distribution to use OAI

pci_dss.reason: OAI ensures that S3 content is only accessed through CloudFront, maintaining security controls.

items.title: ELB/ALB access logs should be enabled for monitoring and audit
items.description: Load balancers without access logs. Cannot audit traffic patterns, identify malicious requests, or troubleshoot issues.
items.remediation: Enable access logs to S3: aws elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-arn ALB_ARN --attributes Key=access_logs.s3.enabled,Value=true Key=access_logs.s3.bucket,Value=BUCKET_NAME Key=access_logs.s3.prefix,Value=alb-logs

pci_dss.reason: This control requires all access to audit trail data be logged. ELB access logs are essential for this.

items.title: API Gateway should have CloudWatch logging enabled
items.description: API Gateway without CloudWatch logs. Cannot track API calls, debug issues, or detect suspicious activity.
items.remediation: Enable CloudWatch logging: Create IAM role with logs:* permissions. Configure stage: aws apigateway update-stage --rest-api-id API_ID --stage-name STAGE --patch-operations op=replace,path=/*/*/logging/loglevel,value=INFO

pci_dss.reason: This control requires logging all access to cardholder data environment. API Gateway logs are essential for this.

items.title: EC2 instances should use IMDSv2 (Instance Metadata Service v2)
items.description: EC2 instances using IMDSv1. Vulnerable to SSRF attacks where attacker can query metadata service and steal IAM credentials.
items.remediation: Enable IMDSv2 requirement: aws ec2 modify-instance-metadata-options --instance-id INSTANCE_ID --http-tokens required --http-put-response-hop-limit 1

pci_dss.reason: IMDSv2 is a security control that prevents credential theft via SSRF attacks.

items.title: Exposed resources should have ownership tags for accountability
items.description: Internet-facing resources without tags identifying owner, application, or environment. Difficult to track responsibility and remediate.
items.remediation: Tag all exposed resources with Owner, Application, Environment: aws ec2 create-tags --resources RESOURCE_ID --tags Key=Owner,Value=NAME Key=Application,Value=APP Key=Environment,Value=prod

pci_dss.reason: This control requires maintaining an inventory of system components. Tags enable easy tracking and reporting.

items.title: Load balancers should redirect HTTP to HTTPS automatically
items.description: ALB/NLB accepting unencrypted HTTP. Users may send sensitive data in plaintext or be intercepted.
items.remediation: Configure listener rule to redirect HTTP to HTTPS: aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn LISTENER_ARN_HTTP --default-actions Type=redirect,RedirectConfig={Protocol=HTTPS,Port=443,StatusCode=HTTP_301}

pci_dss.reason: All traffic to cardholder data environment must be encrypted. HTTP to HTTPS redirect ensures encryption.

items.title: CloudFront should have compression enabled to improve performance
items.description: CloudFront distribution without compression. Larger response sizes, slower performance, increased bandwidth costs.
items.remediation: Enable compression in CloudFront cache behaviors: aws cloudfront update-distribution --id DIST_ID --distribution-config file://config.json (set Compress=true)

pci_dss.reason: Compression is a performance optimization, not directly related to PCI DSS but recommended for best practices.

items.title: Internet-facing resources should follow consistent naming convention
items.description: Resources without consistent naming. Difficult to identify resource purpose, ownership, and environment from name alone.
items.remediation: Adopt naming convention: ENVIRONMENT-APPLICATION-COMPONENT-INSTANCE (e.g., prod-api-alb-01, prod-app-sg-web). Rename existing resources to follow pattern.

pci_dss.reason: Consistent naming contributes to maintaining an accurate and organized inventory.

notes: Comprehensive Internet Exposure Assessment checklist based on AWS Well-Architected Framework Security Pillar and CIS AWS Benchmark. Covers critical to low severity items for identifying resources exposed to internet, mapping architecture chains, and evaluating attack surface. Mapped to PCI DSS v4.0 controls where applicable.
